`tf.data.Dataset.map` with `num_parallel_calls` is known to execute computation in parallel and the instructions provided here are not sufficient to reproduce the issue. 

Please provide a minimal example that can be used to reproduce the issue. As a side note, instead of using `top`, I recommend using `sar` to measure CPU utilization.

@jsimsa I can certainly provide a stand-alone script for that, but just to make sure I didn't get it right:

1. In TensorFlow: `top` shows only 1 process, but `htop` shows multiple threads.
2. In PyTorch, `top` shows multiple processes for the same training.

So, I guess `tf.data.Dataset.map` also does it in parallel, but by using threads instead of different processes? Sorry if the question is stupid, I am not so familiar with these things.
tf.data indeed uses multi-threading as it has lower overhead compared to multi-processing.
@jsimsa Thanks for the confirmation. Let me close this issue.

issue.body:
PR #38473: [xla:gpu] Extract ThunkExecutor out of SequentialThunk

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/38473

`SequentialThunk` has a special meaning in XLA:GPU runtime, and it's confusing as it mixes the "thunk AST" (graph) structure and `Thunk` execution.

Extract the execution bits into `ThunkExecutor` which makes it consistent with `CommandExecutor` counterpart from commands land, and also consistent with XLA:CPU.

In the follow up PR `SequentialThunk` will loose it special meaning in `GpuExecutable`, as the the `executable` must be a `ThunkExecutor` that corresponds to the top level thunk sequence.

This PR is **NFC**, just extracting code into a separate target and updating all users. Longer term we might want to add more "execution optimizations" to executor, i.e. handling multi-stream execution in one central place (similar to how ThunkExecutor in CPU launches tasks into thread pool), today it's spread thin across different individual thunks.
Copybara import of the project:

--
